{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Sources|date=October 2020}}
'''John Alden Thorpe''' (February 29, 1936 – January 18, 2021) was an American mathematician, known for contributions to the field of [[differential geometry]].<ref>''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref>

Thorpe obtained his Bachelor's degree in 1958 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. His Ph.D. was done at [[Columbia University]], under the direction of [[James Eells]] (''Higher Order Sectional Curvature'').<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=10306 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> From 1963 to 1965, he was  ''Moore Instructor'' at MIT and Assistant Professor at [[Haverford College]] in 1965. In 1967 and 1968 he was a visitor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. From 1968, he was Associate Professor and then Professor at the [[Stony Brook University|State University of New York at Stony Brook]] (SUNY). From 1987 he was Professor and Dean at the [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York|State University of New York]] in [[Buffalo, New York|Buffalo]], and from 1993 at [[Queens College, City University of New York|Queens College]] of [[City University of New York]], where he also served as Provost. From 1984 to 1987 he served on the Board of Governors of the [[Mathematical Association of America]]. From 1998 to 2001 he was Executive Director of the [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]].

He and [[Nigel Hitchin]] independently found an inequality between topological invariants, which provides a necessary condition for the existence of [[Einstein metric]]s on four-dimensional smooth compact manifolds. It is now known as the [[Hitchin-Thorpe inequality]].<ref>Thorpe ''Some remarks on the Gauss-Bonnet formula'', J. Math. Mech. 18 (1969), S. 779--786</ref> Thorpe died on January 18, 2021, at the age of 84.<ref>https://www.sunjournal.com/2021/01/24/obituaryjohn-alden-thorpe/</ref>

== Books ==
* Lecture Notes on Elementary Topology and Geometry (with [[Isadore Singer|I.M. Singer]]), Springer Verlag, Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics, 1967
* Linear Algebra, with Applications to Differential Equations (with Paul G. Kumpel), Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1971
* Elementary Topics in Differential Geometry, Springer Verlag, Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics, 1979
* Elementary Linear Algebra (with Paul G. Kumpel), Saunders College Publishing, 1984
